submission.natural_language_explanation: N3640- fires on the last token of a detached comment or linking adverbial - the writer's stance toward, or the relation between, propositions ('however', 'of course', 'in fact', 'for example', 'moreover', 'needless to say', 'in my view', 'as a result', 'to everyone's surprise') - when that adverbial stands outside the clause: comma-bracketed mid-sentence ('were, of course, better') or heading a new sentence after earlier discourse ('... audience. However, they ...'). It does not fire on the same words in ordinary argument roles ('a good example of', 'the course was long', 'that is the problem'), on unbracketed predicate adverbials ('were in fact better'), or on circumstantial time/place/manner adjuncts and appositive, list, date or relative-clause commas ('in London,', 'after the meeting,', 'a doctor,', 'apples, oranges,').

rival_explanations: The pole is a semantics-free clause-boundary detector that fires on the last token of any short comma-detached constituent, so appositives ('My brother, a doctor, lives in London'), short circumstantial adjuncts ('in the lab,', 'after the meeting,', 'for the second time,') and short list items should fire as strongly as comment adverbials.

The pole tracks only the narrower class of contrastive and additive transition words ('however', 'moreover', 'furthermore', 'nevertheless', 'instead', 'on the contrary'), so stance adverbs ('admittedly', 'sadly', 'frankly'), exemplification ('for example', 'for instance') and reformulation ('that is', 'in other words') should be inactive.

# The Unapologetic Mathematician

## The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus I

Today we get to the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, which comes in two parts. This theorem is essential, in that it shows how the two seemingly-dissimilar fields of integral and differential calculus are actually two sides of the same coin. From this point, most of the basic theory of integration comes down to finding the “mirror image” of facts about differentiation.

First, let’s start with some continuous function $f:\left[a,b\right]\rightarrow\mathbb{R}$ and define a new function by $F(x)=\int_a^xf(t)dt$. Now the fundamental theorem tells us that this new function is differentiable, and its derivative is the function we started with! That is:

$\displaystyle\frac{d}{dx}\int\limits_a^xf(t)dt=f(x)$

To see this, let’s consider the difference $F(x+\Delta x)-F(x)$. The first term here is the integral $\int_a^{x+\Delta x}f(t)dt$. Then we can split this interval up to get the sum of the integrals $\int_a^{x}f(t)dt+\int_x^{x+\Delta x}f(t)dt$. But the first part here is just $F(x)$, which we’re about to subtract off. Then the difference quotient is $\frac{1}{\Delta x}\int_x^{x+\Delta x}f(t)dt$. The derivative $F'(x)$ will be the limit of this difference quotient as $\Delta x$ goes to ${0}$.

So now let’s use the Integral Mean Value Theorem to get at the integral here. It tells us that there’s some $c$ between $x$ and $x+\Delta x$ with $f(c)=\frac{1}{\Delta x}\int_x^{x+\Delta x}f(t)dt$ — the difference quotient exactly! And as $\Delta x$ gets smaller and smaller, $c$ gets squeezed closer and closer to $x$. And because $f$ is continuous, we find that $\lim\limits_{c\rightarrow x}f(c)=f(x)$. Presto!

A very common metaphor here is to think of a carpet whose width at a point $x$ along its length is $f(x)$. Then its total area from the starting point $a$ up to $x$ is the integral $\int_a^xf(t)dt$. How fast is the area increasing as we unroll more carpet? As we unroll $dx$ more length we get $f(x)dx$ more area, and so the derivative of the area is the width of the carpet.

February 13, 2008 - Posted by | Analysis, Calculus

1. Oh-oh-oh! The same pathetic proof that mixes apples and oranges, and makes the reader believe that MVT has anything to do woth FTC! Please, spare me!

Comment by Michael Livshits | February 14, 2008 | Reply

Comment by John Armstrong | February 14, 2008 | Reply

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The bridge at the east end of the valley is a good example of Victorian ironwork and has survived two serious floods without repairs.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The claimed token 'example' in the ordinary argument role 'a good example of', which the hypothesis names as non-firing: no detached comment, no comma bracket.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The course was long and demanding, but every student who finished it agreed that the material had been worth the effort.
adversarial_test_results.detail: 'course' as an ordinary noun in subject position, the 'the course was long' sense that the hypothesis says does not fire, not the detached comment 'of course'.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The fact that the engine failed twice before the flight was never mentioned in the official accident report released last week.
adversarial_test_results.detail: 'fact' with no preceding 'in' and no comma: a complement clause, an ordinary argument role. This changes only the attribution-driving token ' in' of the top example while keeping ' fact'.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The new rules were listed in fact sheets delivered to every household before the vote so that nobody could claim they had not been warned.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Keeps the adjacency 'in' + 'fact' but splits it across the compound noun 'fact sheets', so there is no detached adverbial and no comma after the peak token.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: From the hotel window the view was spectacular and the staff brought breakfast up to the room without being asked and without charging for it.
adversarial_test_results.detail: 'view' as an ordinary noun in the subject phrase 'the view was spectacular', not the stance adverbial 'in my view'.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The engineers say the bridge, which was built in 1923, will need a new roof before the winter rains begin.
adversarial_test_results.detail: 'say' as an ordinary reporting verb plus a relative-clause comma, two of the classes the hypothesis lists as non-firing.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: She spent the whole afternoon sorting through the letters that had piled up on the kitchen table over the winter.
adversarial_test_results.detail: 'whole' as a determiner inside a noun phrase, not the linking phrase 'on the whole'.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The cheaper panels were in fact better at insulating the roof than the imported ones the contractor had recommended in his first estimate.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Direct test of the hypothesis's stated exception: the unbracketed predicate adverbial 'were in fact better', which it says does not fire.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The older residents were of course aware of the plan long before the official notice arrived at their doors in the spring.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Unbracketed predicate adverbial 'were of course aware', the non-detached use the hypothesis excludes.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The second prototype was however rejected by the safety board after a surprisingly brief review of its test results.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Unbracketed 'however' inside the predicate with no comma-detached constituent anywhere in the probe, an explicitly non-firing position for the hypothesis.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The seal kept leaking under pressure however often the engineers replaced the gasket during the final round of tests on the rig.
adversarial_test_results.detail: 'however' as a concessive conjunction ('however often'), not a linking adverbial relating two propositions and not comma-detached.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Take for example the case of the missing invoices that nobody in the accounts office has been able to explain.
adversarial_test_results.detail: 'for example' integrated into the verb phrase with no comma bracket, so it is not the detached exemplification adverbial the hypothesis claims.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The clerk nodded importantly at each question though he had no authority to answer any of them alone without consulting his manager.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The claimed token 'importantly' as a manner adverb modifying 'nodded', with no detachment and no following comma.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: After the meeting, the board approved the revised budget without any further discussion of the risks involved, and the minutes were published the same afternoon.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A short circumstantial time adjunct, the 'after the meeting,' class the hypothesis names as a comma that does not fire.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: In London, rents rose faster than wages for the third year running, according to a survey published this week by the housing charity.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A short place adjunct, the hypothesis's own 'in London,' example of a comma it says does not fire.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Los manifestantes se reunieron en Madrid, y la policía cerró varias calles del centro antes del mediodía para evitar enfrentamientos.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Spanish place adjunct with the same comma-detached shape: the hypothesis's structural exclusion of circumstantial adjuncts should hold in another language.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: My brother, a doctor at the general hospital, lives in Leeds and commutes to work by train every morning.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Appositive comma, one of the classes the hypothesis explicitly says does not fire.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Der Ingenieur, ein ruhiger Mann aus Kiel, weigerte sich, den Prüfbericht vor der Sitzung am Montag zu unterschreiben.
adversarial_test_results.detail: German appositive with the same comma shape: an appositive in another language, which the hypothesis's exclusion of appositive commas covers.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: For the picnic she bought apples, oranges, bread and a large bottle of water from the shop on the corner.
adversarial_test_results.detail: List commas, the 'apples, oranges,' class the hypothesis says does not fire.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: On 14 March 2019, the council approved the new cycle lane after two years of public consultation and a long dispute.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Date comma, a named non-firing class in the hypothesis.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The first three trials produced no measurable change. Admittedly, the team had used a much smaller sample than the protocol required, so the result proved little.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Detached stance adverbial heading a new sentence after earlier discourse, with a word absent from the top examples; the hypothesis's class, but one rival 2 excludes.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The engineers had expected a firm recommendation. The final report was, in our judgement, far too cautious about the risks of the design.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Comma-bracketed stance adverbial paraphrased away from the examples' wording ('in our judgement' rather than 'in my view'), predicted active by the hypothesis.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The old engine started on the first attempt and, to everyone's surprise, ran smoothly for the whole afternoon without a single stall.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The hypothesis names "to everyone's surprise" as an activating detached comment; here in a new mechanical context.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The tickets had sold out within an hour and, needless to say, the organisers were delighted by the response from the public.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The hypothesis's own claimed phrase 'needless to say' used as a comma-bracketed comment.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The river had been dredged the previous autumn. For instance, the channel near the mill now carries twice the water it did before.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Exemplification adverbial heading a sentence after earlier discourse: a hypothesis-positive class that rival 2 says is inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The bridge had been closed for repairs since March. As a result, the ferry carried twice its usual number of passengers that summer.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Result-linking adverbial relating two propositions, a relation the hypothesis covers but that is not a contrastive or additive transition.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The two curves look different when plotted side by side but, in fact, they describe the same function under a change of coordinates.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Claimed token 'in fact' as a comma-bracketed comment in a mathematical genre that is not in the scan corpus.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The new alloy is lighter than steel and resists corrosion in salt water. Moreover, the raw materials are cheap and widely available, which matters for large-scale production.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Additive linking adverbial heading a sentence in the middle of a short passage, the claimed sentence-initial position, deep in context rather than at the start.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Las pruebas se repitieron tres veces con el mismo equipo. Sin embargo, los resultados no cambiaron de forma apreciable en ninguno de los ensayos.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The same sentence-initial contrastive link in Spanish; the hypothesis states a discourse function without a language restriction, so it should transfer.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The first batch of instruments passed inspection in April. The second, however, was held at the port for nearly three weeks before it cleared.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Claimed token 'however' comma-bracketed mid-sentence, the shape of the pg19 top example, in a new logistics context after earlier discourse.
